Title

Pico Oscilloscope and Power Supply

Sheet01 / 05
DisciplineElec · SW
ToolsKiCadRaspberry Pi PicoOp-amp front endDMAReactWeb Audio

Task

Build a cheap, easy-to-manufacture oscilloscope that plugs into a laptop over USB, with a built-in power supply. It had to read both positive and negative voltages without damaging the Pico's ADC pins, cap the supply at 30 mA to protect the Pico and the laptop, sample fast, and display in a web browser with a sonification mode that turns the signal into sound.

Actions

  • Sketched the front end on paper, then drew the full schematic and PCB in KiCad.
  • Chose components for low cost and simple assembly while meeting every requirement.
  • Designed and tested the ADC front end: op-amp buffering and voltage scaling, plus a transistor current-limited supply.
  • Extended an existing React app to stream samples from the Pico over serial using DMA, render the waveform live in the browser, and sonify the input voltage.

Results

±5 VSafe input range
42 kS/sSampling rate
5 V · 30 mACurrent-capped supply
< $15Parts and manufacturing
Title

Autonomous RC Car

Sheet02 / 05
DisciplineRobotics
ToolsRaspberry PiROS2PythonLiDARGPSVESCObject recognition

Task

Design and build an autonomous RC car that recognizes and collects three kinds of recyclables: plastic bottles, metal cans and cardboard.

Actions

  • Integrated a Raspberry Pi, LiDAR, GPS, smart camera and VESC motor controller into the car.
  • Implemented object recognition models that detect all three recyclable categories.
  • Wrote Python and ROS2 scripts that turn detections into VESC commands for the steering servo and drive train.

Results

  • Every component runs from the same battery with a clean power distribution layout.
  • The car drives itself and collects recyclables, sorted by category.

Title

Short-Range Radar Detection System

Sheet03 / 05
DisciplineEmbedded
ToolsArduinoUltrasonic sensorServoJavaScriptOnshape

Task

Build a short-range radar from an ultrasonic sensor that sweeps a full 180°.

Actions

  • Designed a mount in Onshape that couples the servo motor to the ultrasonic sensor.
  • Wired and powered the motor and sensor.
  • Wrote an Arduino program to drive the sweep and process readings, and JavaScript for the on-screen display.

Results

  • Detects objects anywhere in the 180° sweep.
  • Shows each object live on screen with its exact angle and distance.
Title · Triton Unmanned Aerial Systems

Wing Ribs and Fasteners

Sheet04 / 05
DisciplineAero · CAD
ToolsOnshapeXFLR5

Task

Design a way to attach the wings of an unmanned aerial system to its mainframe that is quick to assemble and take apart.

Actions

  • Modeled and assembled the ribs and fasteners next to the mainframe in Onshape.
  • Analyzed the airfoil design in XFLR5.

Results

  • Minimal disruption to airflow over the wing.
  • Angled threading keeps the fasteners easy to reach and avoids drilling extra holes in the mainframe.

Task

Add support and stability to a bunk bed frame without drilling into it.

Actions

  • Designed and assembled the bracket and pins in Onshape.
